data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"Counterfactual ordering: if the lease-mismatch refusal guard is the sole enforcement site for a security boundary that external callers can hit (not an internal-only check), it should be Priority 1, not Priority 2. The _reset() guard corrupts the append-only record, but if the record is only consumed internally and never exposed to external callers, while the lease-mismatch refusal is the only thing preventing external access to unauthorized routes, then the security bypass has a larger real-world blast radius than the integrity corruption. The ordering should be: (1) lease-mismatch refusal, (2) _reset() guard, (3) unimported functions, (4) context receipt recovery guard, (5) torn-tail repair, (6) census delta. Justification: external-facing security bypass outranks internal-only integrity corruption when the security boundary is the first line of defense.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the lease-mismatch refusal is an internal-only check (no external caller can reach it), the counterfactual collapses and the default ordering holds.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the _reset() guard's corruption is externally exploitable (e.g., the digest is published and trusted by external consumers), the integrity corruption retains Priority 1 regardless of the lease-mismatch refusal's exposure.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If there is defense-in-depth for the lease-mismatch refusal (another layer also rejects mismatched leases), the security bypass is less severe and the counterfactual does not hold.","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"This counterfactual challenges the default ordering by asking whether the blast radius should be measured by the severity of the corruption or by the exposure surface. If the lease-mismatch refusal is the only thing preventing external callers from hitting unauthorized routes, its death is a live security breach, whereas the _reset() guard's death is an integrity corruption that may only be exploitable by an internal actor with write access to the commit path.
